briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A major point of tension remains the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran and Oman reportedly advancing a plan for maritime fees while Qatar advises temporary suspension of activities. Concurrently, Israeli Defense Minister Katz stated Israel is prepared for an independent "blue and white" operation against Iran and has targets in Iran, while also asserting that US pressure prevented a full-scale Israeli campaign against Hezbollah. Internally, Iran suffered casualties in a "terrorist attack" in Kermanshah, and Israel is grappling with severe internal political division highlighted by incitement against its Chief of Staff and debates over conscription.

IRAN
Iran's Foreign Ministry stated that dialogue with Qatari mediators regarding the implementation of the interim agreement with the United States, including the release of frozen assets, is expected to occur tomorrow, 1 July 2026, in Doha. Qatar's Foreign Ministry confirmed US envoys Steve Whitkoff and Jared Kushner would meet Qatari mediators, but no direct high-level US-Iran meetings are planned, and 6 billion USD of the frozen funds have not yet been transferred, designated for humanitarian goods. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian affirmed mutual adherence to the Islamabad MoU, stating Iran will fulfill its obligations if the US adheres to its commitments. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi also discussed MoU implementation with French counterpart Jean-Noël Barrot.

Militarily, the IRGC conducted an operation in western Iran, killing four "terrorists" and seizing weapons. Separately, two IRGC servicemen, Borhan Krisani and Khalid Khalidi, were martyred in a "terrorist attack" in Paveh, Kermanshah province, on the evening of 29 June. Mohammad Akbarzadeh, Deputy Political for the IRGC Navy, reportedly died in a "car accident" in Kerman. Iran's Acting Defense Minister Majid Ibn Reza vowed a decisive response to any ceasefire violation and expressed readiness to expand defense cooperation with Qatar. The Iranian Army's Rapid Reaction forces on its borders have reportedly deterred ground incursions.

Regarding the nuclear program, Iran's Foreign Ministry stated that the access of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors to damaged nuclear facilities remains blocked, and urged IAEA Chief Grossi to act more responsibly.

Internally, discussions within the Supreme National Security Council regarding the US-Iran MoU reportedly saw President Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, and senior IRGC commanders vote in favor. Preparations are underway for the funeral and farewell ceremonies of the "martyred Leader" (Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei) in Tehran (3 July), Qom (7 July), Karbala/Najaf (7-8 July), and Mashhad (9 July). A hardline newspaper, "Hamshahri," published an image of Donald Trump with a rifle scope on his head, stating "Revenge is inevitable."

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included an airstrike in the central Gaza Strip yesterday, 29 June, killing Ali Qaid Mohammed Stitan, a Platoon Commander in Palestinian Islamic Jihad's (PIJ) elite forces, who participated in the 7 October onslaught. On 28 June, an IDF and Shin Bet strike in southern Gaza killed Talal al-Aal, a PIJ terrorist who held hostages and commanded fighters during the 7 October attacks. The IDF also struck a Hamas tunnel system in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, on 27 June, after identifying attempts to restore it in violation of the ceasefire. Combat engineers sealed a 16-kilometer long Hamas tunnel system in southern Gaza, extending 25 meters deep and featuring 80 rooms, where the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin were held for over a decade. The tunnel ran under civilian sites, including a UNRWA building.

One IDF reservist soldier was severely wounded today, 30 June, at approximately 1:30 p.m., by an explosion during Commando Brigade operations in the village of Arnoun, southern Lebanon; the cause is under investigation.

Israel's short-range Iron Dome air defense system has been upgraded following "extensive series of tests" against a "range of advanced threats," incorporating lessons from the war and operations against Iran. The high-powered laser interception system Iron Beam was also tested alongside Iron Dome. On the home front, fires broke out near Ein Mahel and Yizhar, and a car exploded in Kiryat Haim, killing one person in a suspected criminal incident. Israeli fighter jets were scrambled in response to a false alarm (pilot error) regarding a civilian flight from Warsaw to Ben Gurion Airport, diverting the plane to Cyprus.

Politically, Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel has "no territorial ambitions in Lebanon" but will not withdraw "a millimeter" until Hezbollah is disarmed, adding that the IDF's presence will be "long-term." He claimed that US pressure, particularly from President Trump, prevented a "massive" aerial campaign that "would have dismantled Hezbollah" by linking the Lebanon and Iran arenas. Katz confirmed the Lebanese army refused to enter the Ali Taher Ridge area to clear a Hezbollah tunnel system. He further stated that if Iran attacks Israel with ballistic missiles, the IDF will respond independently and is prepared for an operation named "blue and white," which "could happen even within two days," with targets in Iran.

Internally, widespread condemnation arose from Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Herzog, opposition leaders Gantz and Lapid, and Shas party leadership, regarding "shameful" incitement against the IDF Chief of Staff at a Haredi protest in Bnei Brak. The Attorney General warned against the proposed Haredi conscription law, stating it creates a bypass, and a representative from the IDF predicted 90,000 draft dodgers. A proposed law to prevent the Red Cross from visiting "Nukhba terrorists" in prisons failed due to a Haredi boycott.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF ground operations in Gaza included an airstrike on 27 June against a Hamas tunnel system in central Gaza (Deir al-Balah) that was being reconstructed. Additionally, the IDF successfully sealed a massive 16-kilometer Hamas tunnel network in southern Rafah, located under civilian structures including a UNRWA building, which had been used to hold the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin since 2014.

Casualties reported include the killing of Ali Qaid Mohammed Stitan, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) platoon commander, in central Gaza yesterday (29 June), identified as a participant in the 7 October attacks. On 28 June, Talal al-Aal, another PIJ terrorist involved in the 7 October massacre and holding hostages, was killed in southern Gaza. Unspecified Israeli raids on Gaza resulted in the death of a Palestinian child and her mother, with a child among three killed in Deir al-Balah.

Hamas announced that a delegation led by Zahar Jabareen, head of its West Bank office, arrived in Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials and mediators, focusing on stopping attacks on Gaza, ensuring full aid delivery, and implementing the ceasefire agreement, including a roadmap for phase two and international protection forces. The Palestinian UN envoy called on the international community to take concrete steps to stop Israeli annexation of occupied territories.

LEBANON
An IDF reservist soldier was severely wounded by an explosion today, 30 June, at approximately 1:30 p.m., during Commando Brigade operations in Arnoun, southern Lebanon. The cause of the explosion is under investigation. Israeli warplanes struck the town of Deir Siryan in southern Lebanon.

Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel has "no territorial ambitions in Lebanon" but will not withdraw "a millimeter" until Hezbollah is disarmed. He confirmed that the IDF's presence in Lebanon will be "long-term" and that the Israeli military would not withdraw from "three security zones" in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza. Katz claimed that the Lebanese army refused to enter and clear a major Hezbollah tunnel system under the Ali Taher Ridge, where approximately 30 Hezbollah operatives are believed to be located. He also stated that Israel plans to destroy another major underground Hezbollah system beneath the Beaufort Ridge with "500 tons of explosives." Katz asserted that roughly 600,000 Shiites from southern Lebanon and 700,000 from Hezbollah's Dahiyeh stronghold in Beirut have been displaced, with "almost 100 percent destruction" in border villages in the western and central sectors, and 73% in the eastern sector. No specific Hezbollah operations were reported in the last 24 hours, but Katz noted there are "1,200 Hezbollah operatives from the fence to the Litani." US Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib called for an end to US support for Israeli aggression in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, the Arab League and the Arab Parliament denounced repeated Israeli incursions as blatant violations of Syrian sovereignty. Reports from "NAYA" indicate "Golani gangs" (likely referring to Hayat Tahrir al-Sham) conducted "extermination and abuse" and widespread arrests of Shiites in Al-Mazra'a village in rural Homs, demolishing homes for forced displacement and insulting Imam Hussein. Footage also reportedly shows Israeli forces dancing in cities claimed by "Golani's government" in southern Syria. An IDF soldier's cellphone was reported found in Tal al-Maghar, near Abidin, southern Syria, with the IDF stating the incident is "known and under review." UN forces reportedly entered Abidin, Daraa.

In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi stated that Iraq would not allow its soil to be used for attacks on neighboring countries. A major anti-corruption drive saw Iraqi security forces seize 11 million USD and 4 billion Iraqi Dinars from the home of Adnan al-Jumaili, the Deputy Oil Minister, in Tikrit. Separately, 57 million USD and 27 kg of pure gold were reportedly found in the home of MP Hind al-Abbasi. Security forces conducted raids in Basra, Diwaniya, Arbil, and Baghdad, leading to arrests of officials and individuals suspected of forgery and drug trafficking. The Iraqi Military Intelligence arrested a drug dealer with 4 kg of Captagon in Anbar. Clashes between armed groups and the Iraqi army were reported in Yarmja, Kirkuk. There were reports of an explosion targeting the Lebanese Hospital in Maysan. The Coordination Framework urged its supporters to participate in the funeral ceremony for the "martyred Leader" (Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei) in Iraq, scheduled for 7-8 July.

GULF STATES
Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi expressed support for Iran's plan to impose "maritime service fees" on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz, while also stating that Oman is committed to the freedom of passage in the Strait and that imposing transit fees is internationally prohibited. He noted a common understanding with Iran on the administration of the Strait and affirmed Iran's primary responsibility for ensuring it is free of mine-related hazards. Iran's Foreign Ministry emphasized that the management of the Strait of Hormuz is solely Iran's responsibility. The Qatari Ministry of Transportation advised all maritime vessels to temporarily suspend sailing and other maritime activities.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry announced that US envoys Steve Whitkoff and Jared Kushner would meet with Qatari mediators in Doha, but no direct high-level meetings between American and Iranian officials are scheduled in the coming days. Qatar confirmed that 6 billion USD of the frozen Iranian funds have not yet been transferred, reiterating that these funds are subject to a 2023 agreement for humanitarian goods. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman denied that technical sessions between Washington and Tehran have stopped, with mediators working to facilitate them.

Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Raza Naqvi arrived in Saudi Arabia for discussions on regional developments and joint security coordination.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  An IDF reservist soldier was severely wounded today, 30 June, at approximately 1:30 p.m., by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon.
2.  Israel announced upgrades to its Iron Dome air defense system and tested its Iron Beam laser interception system against advanced threats.
3.  Iran confirmed a technical delegation will meet Qatari mediators tomorrow, 1 July 2026, in Doha to discuss the release of frozen assets, though Qatar states the 6 billion USD has not yet been transferred.
4.  Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated Israel is prepared for an independent "blue and white" operation against Iran and has targets within Iran, warning it "could happen even within two days."
5.  Two IRGC servicemen, Borhan Krisani and Khalid Khalidi, were martyred in a "terrorist attack" in Paveh, Kermanshah province, western Iran, on the evening of 29 June.
6.  The IDF killed two Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) commanders, Ali Qaid Mohammed Stitan and Talal al-Aal, in Gaza on 29 June and 28 June respectively, both implicated in the 7 October attacks and hostage holding.
7.  The IDF completed sealing a 16-kilometer Hamas tunnel system in southern Gaza that ran under civilian structures and had been used to hold the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin.
8.  Iraqi security forces conducted major anti-corruption operations, seizing 11 million USD and 4 billion IQD from the home of Deputy Oil Minister Adnan al-Jumaili, and 57 million USD and 27 kg of gold from MP Hind al-Abbasi.
9.  Widespread condemnations from Israeli political leaders, including Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Herzog, followed "shameful" incitement against the IDF Chief of Staff at a Haredi protest in Bnei Brak.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high in the region. The Israel-Iran dynamic is volatile, with Israeli Defense Minister Katz explicitly stating readiness for independent military action against Iran, including pre-identified targets, should Iran attack Israel with ballistic missiles or if diplomatic efforts fail. Iran's Acting Defense Minister vowed decisive responses to any ceasefire breaches. The Strait of Hormuz continues to be a flashpoint due to conflicting stances from Iran and Oman on maritime fees and navigation rules, exacerbated by Qatar's advisory for a temporary suspension of maritime activities.

The Israel-Lebanon front poses a high risk of escalation, as evidenced by an IDF reservist's severe injury in southern Lebanon and Defense Minister Katz's statements on maintaining a long-term IDF presence to ensure Hezbollah's disarmament and the destruction of its extensive tunnel networks. Ground operations and targeted killings by the IDF in Gaza continue, targeting PIJ and Hamas, indicating ongoing conflict despite ceasefire efforts.

Military postures are shifting, with Israel upgrading its Iron Dome and testing the Iron Beam system, explicitly referencing operations against Iran. Iran maintains its Army's "Rapid Reaction forces" on its borders. Internal security incidents in western Iran, including the "terrorist attack" in Kermanshah, highlight domestic vulnerabilities which could spill over.

Red lines appear to include Israel's determination to prevent Hezbollah's rearmament and attacks from Lebanon, and Iran's insistence on adherence to the Islamabad MoU, particularly regarding its frozen assets and its role in regional security.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** posture involves sending envoys Steve Whitkoff and Jared Kushner to Doha for indirect talks with Iran via Qatari mediators. Defense Minister Katz claimed that US pressure under President Trump linked the Lebanon and Iran arenas, preventing Israel from delivering a "massive" blow to Hezbollah. US Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib called for an end to US support for Israeli "war crimes" in Lebanon, and US Congressman Greg Casar supported cutting military aid to Israel. Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, reportedly described the US-Iran MoU as "just a piece of paper."

Among **Gulf States**, Qatar is actively mediating, facilitating talks between the US and Iran and confirming the status of frozen Iranian assets. The Qatari Ministry of Transportation advised a temporary halt to all maritime activities. Oman's Foreign Minister expressed support for Iran's proposed maritime service fees in the Strait of Hormuz, while simultaneously affirming Oman's commitment to freedom of passage and the international prohibition of such fees, noting Iran's primary responsibility for mine-clearing. Saudi Arabia hosted Pakistan's Interior Minister for regional security coordination.

**European Union members** saw the European Commission provide a 3.9 billion Euro loan to Ukraine for drone production. Fifty members of the European Parliament called for an investigation into FIFA's peace prize awarded to Donald Trump. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi discussed regional developments and MoU implementation with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot.

**Russia** claimed to have intercepted 419 Ukrainian drones, including 61 over Moscow.

**China** is set to receive Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf as a special envoy. The EU and China initiated "Trade and Investment Consultations" to address the EU's significant trade deficit.

**Turkey's** Defense Minister stated the US does not intend to leave NATO but wants European and Canadian allies to assume more responsibility for European security, suggesting Ankara should play a role in European military initiatives.

The **Arab League and Arab Parliament** issued statements denouncing repeated Israeli incursions into Syria as violations of sovereignty.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the reporting. Oman's stance on imposing maritime fees in the Strait of Hormuz is presented contradictorily, with some reports indicating support for Iran's plan while others state Oman's commitment to free passage and the international prohibition of such fees. This ambiguity around a critical chokepoint warrants further clarification.

The status of Iran's frozen assets also shows discrepancies; while Iran's President Pezeshkian reportedly claimed 6 billion USD had been released, Qatar's Foreign Ministry explicitly stated that "until now, 6 billion USD of the frozen Iranian funds have not been transferred to Iran."

Claims made by Israeli Defense Minister Katz regarding the scale of displacement in southern Lebanon (600,000 Shiites, 700,000 from Dahiyeh) and the "100 percent destruction" in certain border villages require independent verification due to their severity. His assertion that US pressure prevented a "massive" aerial campaign to dismantle Hezbollah is also a significant unverified claim.

The death of Mohammad Akbarzadeh, Deputy Political for the IRGC Navy, is reported as a "car accident" by official Iranian sources, but alternative channels suggest it was "sudden and very strange" and linked to his opposition to negotiations, which remains an unverified suspicion. Similarly, the claim that Mojtaba Khamenei cannot attend his father's funeral due to threats is unverified.

Propaganda indicators are present across various sources. Iranian media frequently employs emotionally charged language ("martyred leader," "Zionist crimes") and the "Hamshahri" newspaper's visual threat against Donald Trump is a clear example of aggressive state-aligned messaging. Conversely, Israeli officials' condemnations of internal incitement against the IDF Chief of Staff reflect efforts to manage domestic narratives amidst political division. The report of celebrations in Gaza over Iran's World Cup elimination could be a deliberate attempt to sow discord.

Reporting gaps include the specific details of the "damage" to Iranian nuclear facilities that IAEA inspectors are blocked from accessing, the exact cause of the explosion that wounded an IDF reservist in Lebanon, and any current UNIFIL incidents. The context or specific reasoning for the name "Islamabad MoU" is also not provided.
